title: Fire on Mount Carmel
reflectionQuestion: Elijah trusted God even when he stood all alone. When you need to be brave, who do you like to have beside you?
kidSafetyNotes: NEW anchor (Elijah at Carmel) -- THE Yahweh covenant-name story, the deliberate ~1-in-20 deployment Adam reserved for 'where the name is the point' (first Yahweh since 1811 Burning Bush; 1803 Psalm 23 also has it). Yahweh is introduced GENTLY at the CLIMAX with context ('in the Bible, God's own name is Yahweh') -- the whole story builds to hearing the name, then the people cry 'Yahweh, he is God!'. Default 'God' everywhere else. HARD CONTENT SOFTENED: the prophets of Baal are NOT killed (1 Kings 18:40 omitted) -- they are simply shown to be wrong ('Baal was not real, could not answer'); no taunting cruelty, no slaughter. Flag violence_omitted. Fire here = PROOF/'Yahweh is God' (contrast 1845 Pentecost, where fire = presence/joy -- deliberate same-batch pairing, Adam approved). Indelible image = fire rushing down on the water-soaked altar. Courage model: Elijah brave standing alone, trusting God. VOICE_BRADFORD (passionate conviction).
